subject.title: exec private-LAN access fails while same user GUI/LaunchAgent succeeds

question: Should this issue be resolved by a diagnostic-only exec warning, or should OpenClaw pursue same-user private-LAN reachability parity for gateway-host exec?
rationale: Source inspection can show the missing diagnostic, but allowing, blocking, or documenting private-LAN exec traffic is a security-boundary and product-policy choice.

options.title: Land Diagnostic Only
options.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while keeping broader private-network access semantics in the related security trackers.

options.title: Design Access Parity
options.body: Treat same-user GUI/LaunchAgent reachability as the product goal and require a separate security design before implementation.

options.title: Defer To Broader Policy Work
options.body: Reject the diagnostic-only scope and keep this behavior under the existing private-network policy issues.

recommendation.title: Land Diagnostic Only
recommendation.body: Review and land the open diagnostic PR while keeping broader private-network access semantics in the related security trackers.

likelyOwner.reason: Exec runtime ownership and the broader host-routing/security history most consistently route the policy choice through this owner signal.
